name: Candy Cane Sorrel
grown_as: A small South African bulb, not fully hardy in the UK; best in a well-drained sunny spot or a pot that can be moved under cover in hard frost. Not a true sorrel (Rumex).
habit: A small tufted plant 5 to 15 cm tall from a tiny bulb, short thin stems carrying fine leaves, the flowers held on slender stalks just above.

leaf.arrangement: Clustered near the tops of short thin stems
leaf.type: Compound: three leaflets spreading from the top of a thin stalk
leaf.leaflets: Three, all alike, each very narrow, almost thread-like, notched into two at the tip; often folded along the midrib, and folding down at night
leaf.outline: Each leaflet about 1 cm long and 1 to 2 mm wide
leaf.base: Narrow, meeting the other two at the stalk top

flower.form: A funnel opening to a flat five-petalled face in sun; closed into a tight twisted spiral in dull weather and at night
flower.petals: Five, joined at the base, overlapping and twisted like a furled umbrella
flower.colour: White inside, each petal edged crimson red on the outside, so the closed bud is a red and white spiral like a candy cane
flower.carried: Alone on slender stalks just above the leaves, facing up

winter: The leaves die down after flowering (and are cut down by hard frost outdoors); the small bulbs rest below ground until new growth appears.

leaf: three very narrow leaflets from the top of a thin stalk
each leaflet notched at the tip
bloom: five white petals open flat with a yellow throat
a red edge on the outside of each petal
a closed bud twisted into a red and white spiral
young: a small tuft of short stems with fine three-leaflet leaves
flower: a low tuft of fine leaves
white flowers on slender stalks, with red-and-white spiral buds among them
dormant: little or nothing above ground: small brown bulbs in the soil

look_alikes: Other oxalis such as Oxalis tetraphylla or pink-sorrel (O. articulata) have broad heart-shaped leaflets and pink flowers. Wood-sorrel (O. acetosella) has broad leaflets and white flowers with lilac veins, no red edge. True sorrels (Rumex) are docks with arrow-shaped leaves.
